verdict_reasoning: The bug is reproduced on v16 to v18 and a reviewer confirmed it in message #2, so the goal is not in question. One objection survived, maintenance-fit-1: the thread does not compare this client-side reordering with a server-side WAL reservation in BASE_BACKUP. That is a fixable design point and does not block the idea. What remains is back-patch scope and the exit-time slot drop, which need a committer who knows pg_basebackup.

brief.title: pg_basebackup: create the WAL streaming slot before BASE_BACKUP
brief.problem: With --wal-method=stream, pg_basebackup creates its replication slot only after BASE_BACKUP returns the start position, so a checkpoint in between can remove the needed WAL. The backup then fails with "requested WAL segment ... has already been removed". The author hit this running two pg_basebackup jobs at once from ansible, on v16, v17 and v18.
brief.proposed_design: pg_basebackup opens the WAL streaming connection and creates its slot before it sends BASE_BACKUP, so the slot reserves the WAL from the start. An atexit handler drops the new slot if pg_basebackup exits before the background WAL receiver takes over the connection. New TAP tests use an injection point to hold slot creation, and a bogus --manifest-checksums value to fail BASE_BACKUP after the slot exists.
user_visible_surface: Changed order: the slot used by pg_basebackup --wal-method=stream now exists before BASE_BACKUP starts, so it is visible for longer.
pg_basebackup now drops its new slot on early exit.
author_claims: The race also happens when any session runs a checkpoint, not only a second backup.
Creating the slot first makes it reserve all the WAL the backup needs.
Lingering slots can already happen today; the patch only raises the risk, which the atexit handler addresses.
With --checkpoint=spread the slot stays open longer, which the author lists as a possible caveat.
The author used an LLM to help write the Perl test.
brief.thread_state: Kirill Reshke agreed the bug is real and asked for slot cleanup and a clearer comment; the author then sent v2 in two patches and v3 merged into one. Nobody has replied to v2 or v3, and the author is unsure whether the check in drop_lingering_replication_slot_atexit() is right.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether this is meant for back-patching to v16 through v18.
The proposal does not say how the change behaves with --slot, --create-slot or the temporary slot that pg_basebackup creates by default.
The proposal does not say what the atexit handler does when the connection is already lost, or when the drop itself fails.
The proposal does not say whether a server-side fix was considered, such as BASE_BACKUP reserving WAL before it returns the start position.
Nobody has commented on the Kirill comment fix ("Get a second connection") in v3.

objections.title: Client-side reordering leaves the race for other BASE_BACKUP clients
objections.failure_scenario: An operator runs an older pg_basebackup binary, or a third-party tool that speaks BASE_BACKUP and streams WAL separately, against a patched server. A concurrent checkpoint removes WAL after the start position, and the backup still fails with "requested WAL segment ... has already been removed". The operator finds out only when the backup fails.
objections.argument: The race exists because the server reports a start position without reserving WAL past it, yet the fix lives in one client. Every other client of the replication protocol has to copy the same reordering and the same cleanup logic. The proposal does not say whether a server-side guarantee was considered, such as BASE_BACKUP holding WAL from its start position until the backup ends. Nothing in the thread (messages #1 to #6) compares the two approaches.
objections.author_must_show: Why is a client-side reordering better than having BASE_BACKUP itself keep WAL from the start position, which would also protect older clients and other tools?

critic.reasoning: The patch does not make other clients worse, so the scenario describes today's behaviour. But the thread never compares a server-side WAL reservation with the client-side reordering, and a committer would likely ask for that comparison.

refuted.title: Permanent slot from --create-slot now exists during the start checkpoint
refuted.failure_scenario: A job runs pg_basebackup -X stream --create-slot --slot=s1 --checkpoint=spread, and a timeout kills it with SIGKILL during the spread checkpoint. Slot s1 stays on the primary and holds WAL. Disk fills if max_slot_wal_keep_size is -1, and a rerun fails because s1 already exists.
refuted.argument: Before the patch, a kill during the start checkpoint left no slot. Now a permanent slot exists for that whole window, which can last minutes with --checkpoint=spread, a caveat the author raised in message #1. The atexit handler from message #5 does not run on SIGKILL or a lost host, and Kirill's view that the risk is near zero (message #4) did not cover spread checkpoints. The temporary slot used by default is dropped at disconnect, so only --create-slot is affected.
refuted.author_must_show: For --create-slot, why not create the slot as temporary first, or make it permanent only after BASE_BACKUP succeeds, so a killed client leaves no slot?

critic.reasoning: With --create-slot, a SIGKILL during the copy phase already leaves the permanent slot today, and a rerun already fails on it. The patch adds only the checkpoint window to that exposure, which messages #3 and #4 weighed and accepted as a small added risk.

refuted.title: Back-patch scope and new exit-time slot drop behaviour are undefined
refuted.failure_scenario: The fix is back-patched to v16 through v18 as a bug fix. A user who runs pg_basebackup --create-slot --slot=name finds that a failed run now drops the slot at exit, and their script that reuses the slot on retry behaves differently after a minor upgrade.
refuted.argument: The bug is reported on v16, v17 and v18 (message #1), but the proposal does not say which branches it targets. The default temporary slot already disappears on disconnect, so the atexit handler matters mainly for --create-slot, and that changes user-visible behaviour. The author is unsure whether the handler's check is correct (message #5), and nobody has reviewed v2 or v3. No committer who knows pg_basebackup has engaged.
refuted.author_must_show: Which branches is this meant for, and which slot cases (--slot, --create-slot, the default temporary slot) does the atexit handler change compared with today?

critic.reasoning: Before the patch, a failure before streaming started left no slot. The handler drops only the newly created slot in that same window, so the outcome is unchanged. The unstated target branches and the lack of committer review belong under committability.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The replication slot now exists before BASE_BACKUP starts, so it holds WAL for longer, mainly with --checkpoint=spread.

questions: Why is reordering in pg_basebackup better than having BASE_BACKUP keep WAL from its start position, which would also protect older clients and other tools?
Which branches is this fix meant for: master only, or also v16 through v18?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows pg_basebackup and replication slot handling; none has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The committer signs for changed slot timing in pg_basebackup, possibly on three stable branches, and for an exit-time slot drop whose check the author is unsure about.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review within a day, sent v2 and v3, and registered the CommitFest entry.

priority.reason: The race affects pg_basebackup --wal-method=stream when a checkpoint runs at the wrong moment, and it is reproduced on three releases. The patch is about 13 KiB in one client program plus tests, with no new user-visible option.

precedents_retrieved.title: Changing WAL Header to reduce contention during ReserveXLogInsertLocation()
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Robert Haas, Heikki Linnakangas
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the 8-byte xl_prev field in the WAL record header with a smaller field (first a 2-byte xl_walid from the segment number, later an xl_curr pointer), so ReserveXLogInsertLocation() no longer tracks PrevBytePos. The insertpos_lck spinlock could then become a 64-bit atomic, which cuts contention and shrinks WAL by a few percent.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and others objected that dropping xl_prev removes the check that WAL records form an unbroken chain, which matters for XLOG_SWITCH, timeline switches and the new forward search for checkpoints in pg_rewind. Robert Haas asked to defer the question to the next cycle, and Simon Riggs accepted that on the basis of risk. Heikki Linnakangas then returned it with feedback and asked first to test a 128-bit compare-and-swap (CMPXCHG16B) that keeps the WAL format unchanged.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
Reverted commit(s): Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server Previously, we skipped a checkpoint if no WAL had been written since last checkpoint, though this does not appear in user documentation. As of now, we skip a checkpoint until we have written at least one enough WAL to switch the next WAL file. This greatly reduces the level of activity and number of WAL messages generated by a very low activity server. This is safe because the purpose of a checkpoint is to act as a starting place for a recovery, in case of crash. This patch maintains minimal WAL volume for replay in case of crash, thus maintaining very low crash recovery time.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 18fb9d8d21a28caddb72c7ffbdd7b96d52ff9724.  Per
discussion, it does not seem like a good idea to allow committed changes to
go un-checkpointed indefinitely, as could happen in a low-traffic server;
that makes us entirely reliant on the WAL stream with no redundancy that
might aid data recovery in case of disk failure.

This re-introduces the original problem of hot-standby setups generating a
small continuing stream of WAL traffic even when idle, but there are other
ways to address that without compromising crash recovery, so we'll revisit
that issue in a future release cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the retrieved candidates share keywords only, and no thread message points to an earlier discussion of this idea. Without a prior rejection reason to carry over, the prior-attempts angle has no objection.

From the standards and compatibility angle this is a client-side bug fix with no new syntax, option, GUC, catalog object or dump content. The only user-visible changes are that the slot exists earlier and is dropped on early exit, and both move existing behaviour toward what users already expect. Two points cannot be checked without the code. The first is how --slot and --create-slot interact with the new atexit drop. The second is whether the new order works against older servers that pg_basebackup still supports. A committer would likely ask about both before any back-patch to v16 through v18.
The default temporary slot is dropped on disconnect, and the patch changes no WAL, catalog, protocol or on-disk format. The only persistent-state risk is the permanent slot from --create-slot.

The proposal changes no privilege rules. pg_basebackup already needs a role with REPLICATION, and that role can create and keep slots today. Moving slot creation earlier only makes the slot hold WAL somewhat longer, and the atexit handler drops only the slot it created. A user without replication rights gains no new action and sees no new data. Not checked: what the atexit handler does when the connection is lost, which needs the code.
The bug is real and the change is confined to pg_basebackup, with no hot-path cost for the server. The objections concern where the fix lives and its back-patch scope.

Workarounds exist: run pg_create_physical_replication_slot('name', true) before the backup and pass --slot, or set wal_keep_size. Neither fixes the race in the default --wal-method=stream path, and this is a bug fix in that default path rather than a new feature, so they do not make the change redundant.

This is a bug fix for a reported failure: concurrent pg_basebackup runs fail with "requested WAL segment ... has already been removed", reproduced on v16 to v18 (message #1) and confirmed by Kirill Reshke (message #2). Its costs, such as the slot living longer, fall on pg_basebackup users, so demand is not in doubt.
